Congressional districts are typically redrawn every 10 years.
They were last mapped ahead of the 2022 midterm elections.
But Texas is weighing a change this summer.
Greg Abbott, the move comes after Trump’s Department of Justice sent a letter stating that four districts, held most recently by Democrats, are unconstitutionally racially gerrymandered.
Critics say it’s a ploy for Republicans to hold onto seats in Congress.
We hear from**Jonathan Cervas**, professor at Carnegie Mellon University specializing in redistricting and voting rights.
